title: Digital identity management
competency: Describe digital identity, how it is verified and managed, and the role of Ethiopia's National ID.

keywords.def: All the information about an individual, organisation or electronic device that exists online.
Proving who you are with a body feature such as a fingerprint or face.
Limiting the data you give out, checking and correcting stored data, and avoiding excessive or redundant data.

ideas.name: Digital identity and how it is verified

en.text: A digital identity is a collection of information about a person that exists online; more widely, all the information about an individual, organisation or electronic device online. Businesses use it to identify their clients, and everyone should have a trusted, secure digital identity to reach services such as finance, mobile connectivity, health and education. It is verified by database checks, document verification or biometric verification, such as a fingerprint.

screens.title: Who are you online?
screens.ask: Your physical identity is checked by seeing your face or ID card. How is your digital identity usually checked?
opts: By passwords, codes, database checks or fingerprints
screens.after: Online, nobody sees you, so systems check data: database records, documents or biometrics.

screens.title: Digital identity
paras: onfido.com: "a collection of information about a person that exists online".
Collected together, it creates a digital image of a person.

screens.title: Verifying a digital identity
paras: Database checks: compare details with stored records.
Document verification: check an ID card or passport.
Biometric verification: fingerprint or face (Figure 1.18).
After proving identity, users can access banking, health and travel services online.

screens.text: Every individual should have the right to a trusted and secure digital identity.
Why do businesses collect digital identity information?
How is a digital identity different from a physical identity?
opts: It is made of data that can be copied or stolen, and one person can have many accounts

screens.ans: It is made of data that can be copied or stolen, and one person can have many accounts

ideas.name: Managing your digital identity and the National ID

en.text: Managing a digital identity means limiting the data a person gives out, avoiding excessive storage, checking what data is stored, correcting wrong personal data and avoiding redundant data. It brings organisations both opportunities and risks. In Ethiopia, the National ID project, part of the Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy, is building a robust and reliable digital identification for all Ethiopians and legal residents.

screens.title: Ethiopia's National ID
paras: A national effort improves citizens' digital identity management.
The National ID project is part of the Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy.
It is a robust, reliable digital ID for all Ethiopians and legal residents.
Figure 1.19 shows its fingerprint logo: "National ID", ብሔራዊ መታወቂያ.
It is known as Fayda.

defs: Limiting the data you give out, checking and correcting stored data, and avoiding excessive or redundant data.

screens.clue: Which one makes the data smaller and better?

screens.text: Which actions reduce risks to your digital identity?

a: Share only the data a service needs
screens.why: Limit data and protect access (p.18, Activity 1.6).

screens.text: Ethiopia's National ID project is part of which strategy?

opts: All Ethiopians and legal residents in the country
screens.ans: All Ethiopians and legal residents in the country

screens.text: Which is an advantage of the National ID?
opts: One trusted ID to open bank accounts and get services faster, with less fraud
It replaces the need for any services
It lets anyone use your account
screens.ans: One trusted ID to open bank accounts and get services faster, with less fraud
screens.why: A trusted digital identity opens financial, mobile, health and education services (p.17–18).
screens.clue: What does a trusted ID let you prove?

screens.text: A caller says he is from your bank and asks for the 6-digit code just sent to your phone. What should you do?
opts: Refuse, end the call and report it to the bank
Give the code so he can help
screens.ans: Refuse, end the call and report it to the bank
screens.why: Limit the data you give out (p.18) and examine every request for credentials (p.4).
screens.clue: Would your real bank ask for this?
